title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

interactions.name: peer_influence
interactions.description: Influence on a person's adoption probability from mask-wearing signals of their neighbors weighted by tie strength and susceptibility.

interactions.name: information_broadcast
interactions.description: Broadcast of messages from information sources that update beliefs and perceived benefits/costs of mask-wearing.

interactions.name: policy_enforcement
interactions.description: Mandates and enforcement events that increase adoption probability or penalize non-compliance.

interactions.name: group_norm_feedback
interactions.description: Group-level norms (average adoption) feed back into individual belief updating and thresholds.

interactions.name: tie_rewiring
interactions.description: Dynamic rewiring or adjustment of ties based on homophily, trust, and behavior similarity.

metrics.name: adoption_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of agents wearing masks at each time step and its trajectory over time.

metrics.name: time_to_threshold
metrics.description: Number of steps to reach the specified adoption_target fraction of mask-wearers.

metrics.name: steady_state_adoption
metrics.description: Mean adoption rate over the final observation_window steps.

metrics.name: diffusion_speed
metrics.description: Rate of change in adoption (slope) during the growth phase (e.g., between 10% and adoption_target).

metrics.name: assortativity_of_adoption
metrics.description: Network assortativity/segregation by adoption state, indicating clustering of behavior.

metrics.name: group_adoption_gap
metrics.description: Difference in adoption rates across groups or communities (e.g., max-min or Gini).

metrics.name: behavioral_R0
metrics.description: Average number of new adoptions directly caused by one adopter in the early phase.

metrics.name: exposures_to_adoption
metrics.description: Average number of mask-wearing neighbor exposures before an agent adopts.

validation_criteria.name: convergence_criterion
validation_criteria.description: Convergence if the absolute change in adoption_rate over observation_window is below 0.005.

validation_criteria.name: seed_robustness
validation_criteria.description: Key metrics (steady_state_adoption, time_to_threshold) vary by less than 5% across at least 10 random seeds.

validation_criteria.name: limiting_cases_sanity
validation_criteria.description: With social_influence_weight=0 and policy_effect_size=0, adoption_rate remains near initial_adoption_rate; with very high influence (>=2.0) and low thresholds, near-consensus is reached quickly.

validation_criteria.name: bounds_check
validation_criteria.description: All probabilities and rates remain within [0,1]; adoption_rate within [0,1] at all steps.
